Plus, it seems like they might be using interpolation and temporal consistency, which help blend frames together naturally. And running on a TPU really boosts performance, especially with these optimized diffusion techniques.

comments.author: @davidc8125
comments.text: I tried it out. The biggest obstacle to the current version being used as an engine is object impermanence. I think it needs metadata available relating to what's not currently visible. This isn't easy for training from videos, but I'd think would be relatively possible for synthetic training data. For example an "off screen" permanent inventory and 360 fish eye camera. For larger scale coherence I could imagine a form of RAG. If we could estimate the position and direction of view, you could throw in frames from earlier in the gameplay that look in that direction as extra context for what should be visible.

comments.author: @konstantinavalentina3850
comments.text:
Yes, we're still early days with AI.  Think back to cell phone developmental sophistication, and we're at the equivalent stage of just getting number button alpha-numeric texting.  We haven't even gotten to Flip phone, color display, and are still quite a way away from an "iphone" moment.   
Looking at development this way, seeing where we are, and where we're going, and what could be in a thing even next year or the year after that, and then bigger "moon shot" realizations like AGI, "singularity", SAI, and so on, we're in interesting times.  
Further, unlike simply watching men walk on the moon in grainy black and white low resolution TV, AI is going to proliferate, and be in use almost everywhere.  Some domains will be slow starters, but, like electricity, AI will creep into everyone's lives, and it'll be far more sophisticated than what we have now.  
In less than 10 years, Embodied AI with actually useful robots that do all the chores, housekeeping, upkeep, will be a thing in middle class homes.   
There WILL be mistakes along the way.  Remember Tay, the early AI chatbot that when exposed to the wild wild internet was influenced into becoming a racist, sexist, nazi in a matter of hours?   Mistakes will be made.  
Anyway, this minecraft bot is encouraging.    The real-time modeling of whole worlds could act as predictive modeling overlay for real-world embodied AI to anticipate the real world around it, recognizing variables we may not even notice.  This could also work as a function of next generation AR glasses in allowing the AR glasses wearer to see the world like never before, and even have a sort of "ESP" to predict real world environments for what can be expected.  You can have Spock, or the android Data whispering in your ear that there's  76.2%  probability that the thing is going to do a thing, and your logical course of action would be to do another other thing.
I could be wrong in my predictions about these things.  I have lots of predictions and anticipation regarding our near future in stages close, medium and farther out.  I could be wrong about all of it, but, that's ok.  
Some of what I see, at least the good stuff will certainly be nice should it come.  :)
